paper.title_en: Effects of 80MeV proton irradiation on IHEP-IME LGAD sensors
paper.abstract_en: The shallow-carbon co-implanted Low Gain Avalanche Detector (LGAD), with excellent timing resolution better than 35ps, satisfies the upgrade requirements for ATLAS. To verify the effects of proton irradiation, LGAD with 50µm epitaxy, designed by the Institute of High Energy Physics (IHEP) and fabricated at the Institute of Microelectronics (IME), has been irradiated with 80MeV protons at the China Spallation Neutron Source (CSNS) at three different fluences ranging from 0.8 × 10<sup loc="post">15</sup> neq/cm<math altimg="si1.svg" display="inline" id="d1e594"><msup><mrow/><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> to 2.5 × 10<math altimg="si2.svg" display="inline" id="d1e602"><msup><mrow/><mrow><mn>15</mn></mrow></msup></math> neq/cm<math altimg="si1.svg" display="inline" id="d1e613"><msup><mrow/><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The acceptor removal constant after proton irradiation is measured at <math altimg="si4.svg" display="inline" id="d1e622"><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>3.01</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.45</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">×</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow></msup><mspace class="nbsp" width="0.33em"/><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">cm</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math>, demonstrating strong irradiation resistance of the sensor. Measurements of the I–V and C–V characteristics, collected charge, and timing resolution after irradiation are also presented.
